'''Paul Deheuvels''' (11 March 1948 – 30 January 2026) was a French [[statistician]] and a specialist in [[probability]].<ref name="Festschrift">{{cite book |title=Mathematical Statistics and Limit Theorems: Festschrift in Honour of Paul Deheuvels |date=2015 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |location=Cham |isbn=3319124412}}</ref>

From 1974 to 2013, Paul Deheuvels was a professor of mathematics at the university of [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|Pierre-et-Marie Curie University]] (now [[Sorbonne University]]) in Paris before being appointed [[professor emeritus]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/paul-deheuvels | title=Paul Deheuvels Académie des Sciences}}</ref> He taught probability and statistics.<ref name="Festschrift"/>

Deheuvels was elected Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wayback Machine |url=http://www.lsta.upmc.fr/DEHEUVELS/CV-DEHEUVELS_2010.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029105644/http://www.lsta.upmc.fr/DEHEUVELS/CV-DEHEUVELS_2010.pdf |archive-date=29 October 2020 |access-date=20 October 2025 |website=www.lsta.upmc.fr}}</ref> in 1985, and Member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-D/paul-deheuvels.html}}</ref> He was also a member of the  [[International Statistical Institute]] (ISI), and a foreign corresponding member of the Royal Academy of Exact, Physical and Natural Sciences of Spain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|url=https://rac.es/sobre-nosotros/miembros/academicos/correspondiente-internacional/}}</ref>

== Education ==
Deheuvels completed his secondary education at [[Lycée Lakanal]] in [[Sceaux, Hauts-de-Seine|Sceaux]], France, at the age of 17. After preparatory classes in mathematics at [[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]], he was admitted in 1967, at the age of 19, to the [[École Normale Supérieure]], rue d’Ulm.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Paul+Deheuvels. | title=L'Annuaire &#124; a-Ulm | access-date=11 September 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150520151458/http://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Paul+Deheuvels. | archive-date=20 May 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Research ==
Deheuvels' work was in the fields of [[extreme value theory]], [[empirical processes]], [[nonparametric estimation]] of tails and tail indices, extreme dependence and extreme [[copula (statistics)]].<ref name="Festschrift"/>

== Séralini affair ==
The [[Séralini affair]] was the controversy surrounding the publication, retraction, and republication of a [[journal article]] by French [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] [[Gilles-Éric Séralini]]. The study was criticized by various regulatory authorities and scientists prior to retraction. With few exceptions, the scientific community dismissed the study and called for a more rigorous peer-review system in scientific journals.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Martinelli|first1=L|last2=Karbarz|first2=M|last3=Siipi|first3=H|title=Science, safety, and trust: the case of transgenic food.|journal=Croatian Medical Journal|date=February 2013|volume=54|issue=1|pages=91–6|doi=10.3325/cmj.2013.54.91|pmid=23444254|pmc=3584506}}</ref> Deheuvels was one scientist who supported the study.

== Death ==
Deheuvels died on 30 January 2026, at the age of 77.<ref>[https://carnetdujour.lefigaro.fr/deces/annonces/618275300/ Paul Deheuvels] {{in lang|fr}}</ref>

== Books ==
* L’Intégrale, Presses Universitaires de France, 1980 (ISBN 2130366481).
* La recherche scientifique, Que sais-je?, 1990 (ISBN 9782130432418).
* Lectures on Empirical Processes: Theory and Statistical Applications, EMS Series of Lectures in Mathematics, 2007.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://ems.press/books/elm/223. | title=Paul Deheuvels – Lectures on empirical processes}}</ref>
* Probabilité, Hasard et Incertitude (Que sais-je ?), PUF, 2008 (ISBN 9782130571254).
